extracted.intended_audience: NIH-funded researchers and institutional research administrators preparing grant applications
extracted.subtask_short: nih data management and sharing plan
extracted.subtask_description: Writing an NIH Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan to include required elements and satisfy the NIH policy (effective dates and updated elements as noted). Applies to data management and sharing language submitted with NIH grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 1: Data Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of scientific data to be generated; Estimated amount of data; Data types subject to sharing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what scientific data will be created, give an estimated volume/size where possible, and note which data types will be subject to sharing. Be specific about categories (e.g., raw, processed, metadata) so reviewers can judge scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 2: Related Tools, Software and/or Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools needed for accessing or manipulating data; Open vs. proprietary; Sustainability of any custom-developed tools
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify software, code, algorithms, and tools required to use the data. State whether they are open-source or proprietary and describe plans for sustaining or providing access to custom tools (e.g., repository, documentation, maintenance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 3: Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and metadata standards to be applied; Common data elements; File formats compatible with standards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare the standards (ontologies, metadata schemas, controlled vocabularies) you will apply and the file formats you will use. If there are community or domain standards, state them explicitly and explain how they will be used to ensure interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 4: Data Preservation, Access, and Associated Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository where data will be archived; Persistent unique identifiers (DOIs); Time period of data availability; Access procedures and any restrictions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the repository (or repository type) intended for archiving, how you will assign persistent identifiers, how long data will remain available, and detailed access procedures including any embargoes or restrictions and the rationale for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 5: Access, Distribution, or Reuse Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated limitations on data sharing; Plans for protecting privacy and confidentiality; Whether data will be controlled access vs open
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe foreseeable legal, ethical, technical, or other limits to sharing; steps to protect participant privacy, confidentiality, and intellectual property; and whether data will be open access or placed under controlled-access mechanisms (and how access requests will be handled).

rubrics_metrics.name: Element 6: Oversight of Data Management and Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: How compliance will be monitored; Who is responsible for compliance; Frequency of internal review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify personnel or roles responsible for implementing and monitoring the plan, describe monitoring procedures (e.g., internal review cycles), and indicate how frequently the plan and practices will be reviewed and updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated Elements (effective May 25, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH released NOT-OD-26-046 with Updated Elements of an NIH Data Management and Sharing Plan. The new elements are mostly yes/no questions plus a table listing data types and repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications on or after May 25, 2026, complete the updated elements which include structured yes/no questions and a data-type/repository table. Ensure the DMS plan format aligns with the updated form fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes/No Question: Maximum appropriate sharing of scientific data
rubrics_metrics.description: Will there be maximum appropriate sharing of scientific data underlying peer-reviewed publications and other findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer yes/no as required in the updated elements and be prepared to justify the response in the plan text (e.g., limitations, embargoes, legal or privacy constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes/No Question: Timing of sharing for data underlying peer-reviewed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific data underlying peer-reviewed publications be shared by the time of publication or by the end of the period of performance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether data will be released at publication or by project end; align timelines with journal and repository policies and explain any deviations or embargoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes/No Question: Minimum duration of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Will shared scientific data be made available for at least as long as required by applicable data repository policies and/or journal policies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm compliance with repository- and journal-specific retention requirements; if retention will be shorter or longer, explain justification and mechanisms for long-term preservation (e.g., chosen repository's policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: DMS Plan as Award Term and Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a grant is awarded, the DMS Plan becomes part of the award's terms and conditions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the submitted DMS plan is binding as a condition of the award; plans should therefore be realistic, implementable, and consistent with institutional practices and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance review and updating
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects researchers and institutions to implement data management and sharing practices as described; Compliance reviewed during regular reporting intervals (annual RPPR); Plan can be updated during the project
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for NIH to review compliance during progress reporting (e.g., RPPR). Include mechanisms to update the DMS plan as project circumstances change and document changes appropriately in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository selection and FAIR principles
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-recommended generalist repositories; Domain-specific repositories (dbGaP, GEO, ClinicalTrials.gov, etc.); NIH supports sharing in repositories that follow FAIR principles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an appropriate repository (domain-specific when available) and ensure it supports FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles. Provide repository names and, when applicable, accession or persistent identifiers, and justify repository choice relative to data types.
